headline: The daemon keeps reconnecting while the server is down and resolves server names through the system resolver
summary: Two faults could stop a daemon from syncing until someone restarted it. Wherever the file watcher polls, the container image included, the daemon exited with status 0 as soon as its connection to the server dropped. A server named by a Docker service name, an /etc/hosts entry or a name that exists only on the local network was never reached, because the framework resolved hostnames through a public DNS-over-HTTPS resolver. Both are fixed, and the vendored framework moves from blamejs 0.20.1 to 0.21.4, which checks every TLS server's certificate chain up to a trust anchor and refuses certificates whose private key is publicly known. To upgrade, install the new binary or pull the new image. The configuration file and the state database carry over unchanged.

items.title: The daemon keeps running while the server is unreachable
items.body: With the poll file watcher, which the container image uses and which `HERMITSTASH_WATCHER_MODE=auto` picks for network and virtualized mounts, nothing held the daemon's process open between reconnect attempts. When the server restarted, crashed or could not be reached at startup, the daemon exited with status 0 instead of reconnecting, and a container whose restart policy does not restart after a clean exit stayed stopped. The daemon now keeps running and reconnects with its usual backoff. If its event loop ever drains, it logs `The event loop drained while the daemon was running` before it exits.

items.title: Server names resolve through the operating system's resolver
items.body: The framework sent every hostname outside a few local suffixes to a public DNS-over-HTTPS resolver, so a server named by a Docker service name, an `/etc/hosts` entry or a name that exists only on the local network was never reached, and the daemon treated the failure as permanent and stopped reconnecting. The client now resolves the server and the release download host through the operating system's resolver, and a name that does not resolve is retried with backoff. Set `BLAMEJS_DNS_TRANSPORT=doh` or `BLAMEJS_DNS_TRANSPORT=dot` to resolve through DNS over HTTPS or DNS over TLS instead. A WebSocket dial that fails before the server answers is now logged as such, not as `Server rejected the WebSocket upgrade (HTTP 0)`.

items.title: A connection the server drops is noticed at once
items.body: When the server process went away without closing the WebSocket, after a crash or an out-of-memory kill for example, the client noticed only when the 90-second heartbeat deadline passed. It now reconnects as soon as the connection closes, and logs `WebSocket connection lost` at info level.

items.title: Self-update completes on slower links
items.body: The self-update download stopped after two minutes whatever its progress, so a release binary of 107 to 140 MB never finished on a link slower than about 7 to 9 Mbit/s, and the failure was logged as `HTTP 200`. The download now allows for 128 KiB/s over its size cap, about 34 minutes for the 256 MiB cap, and still stops after one minute without progress. A download that fails after the transfer started is logged with its actual reason, and a connection reset or a body that ends short is retried up to three times. A partial download is never kept.

items.title: Error messages carry the server's reason
items.body: When the server refuses an upload, a download or a delete, the error carries the `detail` of its RFC 9457 problem response, its `title` when the server withholds the detail, or the `error` field of an older server's response. An upload or download error previously carried the whole response body, and a delete error carried only the HTTP status. A refused upload whose error body is too large to read keeps its HTTP status, so a 4xx refusal is not retried. A field in an error body that is not a string no longer turns into `[object Object]` or an exception.

items.title: A failed encrypted rename names the likely cause
items.body: When the server rejects a file rename again after a fresh session, the error now says that the server refuses a request whose timestamp is more than 5 minutes from its own clock, and to check this machine's clock. A reverse proxy's error page in place of the server's answer is reported with its HTTP status as a proxy error, not as a JSON parse error.

items.title: A state database the integrity check cannot read is kept
items.body: At startup the daemon checks its state database with `PRAGMA integrity_check`. Any error from that check counted as corruption, so a check that could not run, for example because of a transient I/O error, renamed the database aside and started the daemon on an empty one. Only a database SQLite reports as damaged is set aside now. A check that cannot run stops the start with `localdb-thin/integrity-check-failed` and leaves the file in place.

items.title: Log rotation on Windows no longer drops records
items.body: When another program held the log file open without delete sharing, which some Windows log viewers do, every log line blocked the daemon for about 160 ms and was then dropped while the rotation kept failing. The daemon now keeps writing to the active file, logs one `rotate-failed` warning, and retries the rotation every 5 seconds. Two rotations in the same second no longer overwrite each other's archive.

items.title: Clock checks warn earlier and honor BLAMEJS_NTP_REQUIRE_REACHABLE
items.body: The startup clock check warns from one minute of drift, where it warned from five, and the warning names the server's 5-minute limit on encrypted requests. When no time server answers, the daemon starts with a warning by default. `HERMITSTASH_NTP_STRICT=1` or `BLAMEJS_NTP_REQUIRE_REACHABLE=1` makes it refuse to start instead, and the refusal names the variable that caused it.

items.title: File rename works with HermitStash v1.15.7 and later
items.body: File rename uses the server's per-session encrypted envelope and works with a server built on blamejs 0.20.1 or later, which is HermitStash v1.15.7 and later. The README previously stated that it needed a server on the same blamejs minor line as the client.

items.title: The poll watcher yields between directories
items.body: After the first scan, each poll of the sync folder hands the event loop back between directories, and the next poll is timed from the end of the previous one. On a slow mount, such as a Docker Desktop bind mount, a large folder previously kept the daemon busy from one scan to the next. The first scan at startup still reads the whole tree in one pass.

items.title: Server certificates are checked up to a trust anchor
items.body: Every TLS connection the client opens, to the HermitStash server and to the release download host, now checks the server's certificate chain up to a trusted root and refuses a certificate whose private key is publicly known. A refusal is logged with `tls/server-chain-unverifiable` or `tls/compromised-key`. The check also applies when `pinnedServerSpki` or tunnel mode is set: the pin is checked in addition to the chain, not in place of it. A server certificate issued by the HermitStash CA or by a public CA passes unchanged.

items.title: The WebSocket client limits fragments per message
items.body: The framework's WebSocket client now limits how many fragments one incoming message may arrive in, in addition to the limit on its size. With the 8 MiB size limit this client sets, a message may arrive in at most 131072 fragments. When a server exceeds that, the client drops the connection, logs `incoming message exceeds the maximum fragment count (131072)`, and reconnects with its usual backoff. A HermitStash server sends each sync event as a single frame.

items.title: Vendored blamejs moves to 0.21.4
items.body: The vendored framework moves from 0.20.1 to 0.21.4, and its nested certificate toolkit moves from 0.7.37 to 0.9.7. If setting the pragmas or creating the tables fails while the state database opens, the framework now closes the database before it reports the error, so the file is not left locked on Windows. When the client runs from source with `node bin/hermitstash-sync.js`, the startup vendor integrity check now refuses a manifest entry that has no file path or no recorded hash, where it previously skipped that entry. The released binaries and the container image do not run this check.

items.title: The release build uses pinned esbuild and postject
items.body: The release workflow installs esbuild 0.28.2 and postject 1.0.0-alpha.6 from `package-lock.json`, with their integrity hashes checked and install scripts skipped, and `build/build-sea.js` calls them through their JavaScript APIs. The build previously ran both through `npx --yes`, which fetched whatever version npm resolved at build time. The build also stops if the bundle includes any file from `node_modules`. To build locally, run `npm ci --ignore-scripts`, then `node build/build-sea.js`.

items.title: Container bases and action pins move to their current releases
items.body: The `cgr.dev/chainguard/wolfi-base` runtime base moves to its 2026-10-24 digest and the build-stage `node:24.21.0-slim` image to its 2026-10-06 digest. The Docker build, Buildx, QEMU and login actions, the setup-node, setup-python and artifact actions, and the CodeQL actions move to the latest release within their current major version.
